terms.comment: domī, at home; domum, homeward; domō, from home.

phrases.latin: Culīnam habet, cubicula, inter quae hospitium est, balneum, lātrīnam, hortum, trīclīnium, exedram; vestibulum parvum, ubi calceī exuuntur, soccī induuntur, paenulae ex uncīs pendent
phrases.english: It has a kitchen, bedrooms (one of them a guest room), a bathroom, a toilet, a garden, a dining room, a sitting room; a small front hall where shoes come off, slippers go on and coats hang from hooks (of Grandpa’s house)
phrases.source: Libellus III, Apud avum et aviam

sources: Lewis & Short: domus
Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word.
